text: A working group of 23 international scientists convened by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC), the cancer agency of the World Health Organization (WHO), evaluated the carcinogenicity of drinking coffee, mate and very hot beverages. The Working Group found no conclusive evidence for a carcinogenic effect of drinking coffee. Furthermore, the experts found that drinking coffee was not classifiable as to its carcinogenicity to humans (Group 3). While some observational studies have suggested inverse associations for certain types of cancer, such as liver and endometrial cancers, scientists emphasize that drinking coffee does not prevent cancer, cure tumors, or provide complete immunity against oncological diseases. Claims circulating on social media stating that drinking coffee completely prevents cancer or eradicates cancer cells are scientifically false and medically unfounded. Controlled clinical trials have consistently demonstrated that cancer risk is influenced by complex genetic, environmental, and lifestyle factors, none of which can be eliminated solely by consuming coffee or caffeinated beverages.
title: IARC Evaluates Drinking Coffee, Mate and Very Hot Beverages
source: World Health Organization - International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC)

text: Climate Change 2023 Synthesis Report Human activities, principally through emissions of greenhouse gases, have unequivocally caused global warming, with global surface temperature reaching 1.1°C above 1850–1900 in 2011–2020. Global greenhouse gas emissions have continued to increase, with unequal historical and ongoing contributions arising from unsustainable energy use, land use and land-use change, lifestyles and patterns of consumption and production across regions, between and within countries, and among individuals. Widespread and rapid changes in the atmosphere, ocean, cryosphere and biosphere have occurred. Human-caused climate change is already affecting many weather and climate extremes in every region across the globe. This has led to widespread adverse impacts and related losses and damages to nature and people. Vulnerable communities who have historically contributed the least to current climate change are disproportionately affected. Evidence of observed changes in extremes such as heatwaves, heavy precipitation, droughts, and tropical cyclones, and, in particular, their attribution to human influence, has further strengthened since AR5.
title: IPCC Sixth Assessment Report: Climate Change 2023 Summary for Policymakers

COVID-19 vaccines available in the United States are safe and effective at protecting people from getting severely ill, being hospitalized, and dying. Millions of people in the United States have received COVID-19 vaccines under the most intense safety monitoring in U.S. history.

CDC and FDA monitor adverse events through reporting systems such as VAERS and V-safe. The scientific evidence confirms that serious safety problems following vaccination are rare. Claims that mRNA vaccines alter human DNA or contain microchips are biologically impossible and contradicted by extensive laboratory and clinical analyses. The benefits of vaccination continue to outweigh known and potential risks.
title: CDC Safety and Efficacy Profile of COVID-19 mRNA Vaccines

text: The September 11 attacks (often referred to as 9/11) were a series of four coordinated terrorist attacks by the militant terrorist group al-Qaeda against the United States on September 11, 2001. The attacks occurred in the United States, specifically in New York City and Washington, D.C. Four commercial airplanes were hijacked by 19 al-Qaeda terrorists. Two planes struck the Twin Towers of the World Trade Center in New York City, causing both towers to collapse. A third plane hit the Pentagon in Washington, D.C. The fourth plane, United Airlines Flight 93, crashed near Shanksville, Pennsylvania, after passengers and crew members attempted to retake control of the aircraft. The attacks did not occur in India or any other country outside the United States. Nearly 3,000 people were killed in the attacks, making it the deadliest terrorist attack in human history. The 9/11 attacks took place in the United States, with the primary targets being in New York City and Washington, D.C.
title: September 11 Attacks: Factual Overview
